summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, and polysubstance use, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, cough, and wheeze over three weeks, consistent with a COPD exacerbation. He was tachypneic and hypoxic on arrival, with rapid atrial fibrillation managed with IV and oral metoprolol. Initial concern for infection led to broad antibiotics, but the chest X-ray showed no pneumonia, and antibiotics were de-escalated. He was treated with systemic steroids, nebulizers, and transitioned from fluticasone to Advair for better COPD control. His breathing improved, and he was discharged on room air. Urine toxicology revealed cocaine use, prompting counseling on cardiovascular risks. He was discharged home with a five-day course of prednisone and azithromycin, and instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.
